outcome: intraoperative complications (e.g., vascular injury, ureter injury, retroperitoneal hematoma)
postoperative complications within 90 days (e.g., urinary tract infection, revision of abdominal scar, ileus, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism)
cohort: The study included 660 consecutive patients undergoing Anterior Lumbar Interbody Fusion (ALIF) with or without a history of prior abdominal surgery between 2008 and 2018 at a single tertiary center, excluding those under 18, with spinal malignancy, or ALIF above L3.
finding: The study found that each additional prior abdominal surgery increased the odds of developing an intraoperative complication by 52%, but neither the type nor the number of prior abdominal surgeries significantly predicted postoperative complications.
